items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 10, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Trane did. ... And that kind of like influenced me you know.

ctx.x: When you first arrived it was frightening to you, like did you go to a rehearsal first or did you just land in a gig?
Oh when I first moved to New York I started working with Grant Green. Guitarist for Blue Note Records, he played bebop guitar. And he had Bob Cranshaw, Bob © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Cunningham and Ben Dixon on drums and on tour instead he got an organ. Then sometimes we would play gigs with an organ. And then I got gigs with Hank Crawford. Now this was ’63. But meanwhile I would take little gigs with Sun Ra, with John Gilmore playing saxophone. Actually John Gilmore had went with Trane — I mean Art Blakey. He went with Art Blakey. And Sun Ra was using Pharoah but Trane was calling him all the time. John Coltrane was calling him all the time. So there I was, about the same age. So they tried…

items.title: Wendell Harrison interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 17, 2022 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee narrates that Pharoah Sanders worked with John Coltrane ('he was working with Sun Ra and then around different groups and then John Coltrane, he was hanging out with John Coltrane. John liked him... he started touring'), but the interviewee (Wendell Harrison) only mentions Coltrane i

ctx.x: Kiwami. K-I-N-I-B-I [misspelled] Ziwati. And we were staying together in the loft on Broadway, 89 E Broadway Street. And all kinds of people would come by and sessions, and we studied, actually we were vegetarians at the time. And so he called Kiwami to come in and play for a few gigs and whatnot, and Sun Ra asked Kiwami did he know of a saxophone player. So Kiwami recommended me, because Pharoah had went with — Pharoah was doing presentations and performances with Sun Ra as well, but he had worked with Trane.…

from Alabama basically, by way of Chicago. So I didn’t really eat that much because I was so excited about playing with the group that I’d never played that way before. I’d never played that free style before you know. So when I started playing he told me to forget about changes, just think about the sound and imagery you know. Let your imagination take control.
